extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, owners/operators of electric generating units (EGUs), and other regulated stakeholders (industry, RTO/ISOs, NGOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluation criteria for state plans and affected EGUs under the EPA's Carbon Pollution Standards for steam generating EGUs, including increments of progress, reporting milestones, monitoring and CCS-specific reporting, and allowable compliance flexibilities. Focused on what states must include in plans and what EGUs must document and report to demonstrate progress and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF-based compliance date extension (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: States may provide a compliance date extension of up to 1 year for certain affected EGUs when add-on control technologies are required and installation is delayed due to circumstances outside the affected EGU's control; for longer extensions the state may revise its plan based on Remaining Useful Life (RULOF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To demonstrate a fundamental difference between the EGU's circumstances and the EPA's basis for the emission guideline compliance schedule, the state should provide documentation justifying why it is unreasonable for the affected EGU to meet the compliance schedule even with a 1-year extension, based on one or more considerations in 40 CFR 60.24a(e)(1). Documentation should show the delay was due to circumstances outside the EGU's control and that the EGU met all relevant increments of progress and obligations in a timely manner. Documentation such as permits obtained and/or contracts entered into, receipts, invoices, and correspondence with vendors and regulators is helpful evidence. The state must demonstrate the need to invoke RULOF was not caused by self-created circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: RULOF—'no longer than necessary' requirement for longer schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing a longer compliance schedule pursuant to 40 CFR 60.24a(f)(1), a state must demonstrate that the revised schedule is no longer than necessary to accommodate the circumstances that caused the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state must justify that additional time requested beyond the optional 1-year extension is strictly necessary to address circumstances outside the EGU's control; supporting evidence should be provided as with RULOF generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include Increments of Progress (IoPs) when compliance deadline exceeds threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include legally enforceable Increments of Progress (IoPs) toward compliance for each designated facility when the final compliance deadline is more than the threshold specified in subpart Ba (20 months after plan submittal under the revised subpart Ba); these emission guidelines adopt a 24-month plan submittal deadline and compliance dates that exceed the 20-month threshold, triggering IoPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IoPs are used to assure steady progress toward compliance and provide transparency given lengthy planning and construction timelines for BSERs like CCS and natural gas co-firing. States must include IoPs for affected units in medium-term and long-term coal-fired subcategories (and tailor IoPs to BSER where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology-specific IoPs tailored to BSER
rubrics_metrics.description: For units complying through BSERs that involve installation of emission controls (long-term: CCS; medium-term: natural gas co-firing), IoPs must be tailored to the specific BSER; units using different control technologies must adopt increments corresponding to the steps in 40 CFR 60.21a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some IoPs have been adjusted to align with planning, engineering, and construction steps anticipated for CCS or natural-gas co-firing, but retain the basic structure of subpart Ba IoPs. Units not adopting the subcategory BSER must particularize the subpart Ba generic IoPs as appropriate for their control strategy. Natural gas- and oil-fired EGU subcategories (BSER = routine O&M) are exempt from IoP requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State discretion and constraints for assigning calendar dates to IoPs
rubrics_metrics.description: States may choose calendar dates for each IoP for long- and medium-term coal-fired EGUs, subject to specified constraints: the IoP for submittal of a final control plan must be the earliest deadline among increments; the IoP for final compliance must align with the subcategory compliance date (Jan 1, 2032 for long-term; Jan 1, 2030 for medium-term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach provides flexibility to account for facility-specific planning while ensuring the first and final increments are anchored. States have discretion to set dates based on unique circumstances, and may allow simultaneous work on separate increments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional IoPs for pipeline construction and sequestration identification
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include additional IoPs specific to pipeline planning, permitting, and construction for long- and medium-term coal-fired subcategories, and an additional IoP related to identifying an appropriate sequestration site for the long-term coal-fired subcategory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These increments ensure timely progress on pipeline activities required to enable full compliance. For sequestration identification, the IoP addresses locating where CO2 will be injected and how it will be transported and permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting requirement for IoPs and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must require affected EGUs with IoPs to post the activities/actions that constitute each increment, the schedule required in the state plan for achieving them, and, within 30 business days, any documentation necessary to demonstrate achievement, to the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posting requirement is intended to provide transparency and timely public access to evidence of progress; see section X.E.1.b.ii of the preamble for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven IoPs for long-term coal-fired units adopting CCS
rubrics_metrics.description: For long-term coal-fired steam generating units adopting CCS, seven enforceable IoPs must be included in the state plan: (1) submission of a final control plan; (2) awarding contracts or issuing purchase orders for emission control systems or process modifications; (3) initiation of onsite construction/installation to achieve 90% CO2 capture annually; (4) completion of onsite construction/installation to achieve 90% CO2 capture annually; (5) demonstration that all pipeline permitting actions have commenced (with specific evidence); (6) submittal of a report identifying geographic sequestration location, transport, regulatory requirements, and timeline; (7) final compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final control plan must be consistent with subcategory declaration and include supporting analysis (feasibility and/or FEED study), anticipated timeline, and benchmarks. Demonstration of pipeline permitting commencement must include planning/design documentation, list of pipeline-related permit applications, attestation the list is complete, and a timeline to complete permitting activities. States must assign calendar deadlines so that the first increment is the earliest and the seventh increment is set for Jan 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoPs for long-term units not adopting CCS must follow 40 CFR 60.21a(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired long-term units adopting a compliance approach that differs from CCS must have state-adopted IoPs consistent with the IoPs at 40 CFR 60.21a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with CCS-adopting units, states must assign calendar deadlines with the first increment (submittal of final control plan) earliest and the final increment set for Jan 1, 2032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six IoPs for medium-term coal-fired units adopting natural gas co-firing
rubrics_metrics.description: For medium-term coal-fired units adopting natural gas co-firing, six enforceable IoPs must be included in the state plan: (1) submission of a final control plan (including design basis, timeline, benchmarks); (2) awarding contracts or purchase orders for boiler modifications; (3) initiation of onsite construction/installation for 40% annual-average natural gas co-firing; (4) completion of onsite construction for 40% co-firing; (5) demonstration that pipeline permitting actions have commenced (with specified evidence); (6) final compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must set deadlines so the first increment (final control plan submission) is the earliest and the sixth increment (final compliance) is set for Jan 1, 2030. Demonstration of pipeline permitting commencement must include planning/documentation, list of permit applications, attestation of completeness, and timeline to complete permitting activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: IoPs for medium-term units not adopting natural gas co-firing must follow 40 CFR 60.21a(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coal-fired medium-term units adopting a compliance approach other than natural gas co-firing must have IoPs consistent with the increments in 40 CFR 60.21a(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must assign calendar deadlines so the first increment corresponds to 40 CFR 60.21a(h)(1) as the earliest and the final increment corresponds to 40 CFR 60.21a(h)(5) and is set for Jan 1, 2030.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of IoP dates when compliance date extension approved
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affected EGU receives approval for a compliance date extension, at least one IoP (and possibly several) must be adjusted to align with the revised compliance date; the new IoP dates must be specified in the extension application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA notes the last increment—final compliance—should be no later than 1 year after the original compliance date per section X.C.1.d. Plan revisions and the compliance date extension mechanism permit IoP modification to align with approved extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of state plan revision process for changes (40 CFR 60.28a)
rubrics_metrics.description: States may use the subpart Ba plan revision process, including RULOF-based adjustments and revisions to subcategory assignments and corresponding IoPs, to account for changes in planned compliance approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan revisions are available at a state's discretion to account for changes in planned compliance, including switching subcategories or altered implementation timelines due to unforeseen circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting obligations and milestones for EGUs planning permanent cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs that plan to permanently cease operations (applicable to medium-term subcategory and units invoking RULOF based on remaining useful life) must submit an Initial Milestone Report five years before the planned cessation date, annual Milestone Status Reports for each intervening year, and a Final Milestone Status Report no later than six months after the committed cessation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reporting framework is intended to provide transparency and assurance that EGUs progressing toward a commitment to cease operations are on-track, to protect the integrity of subcategory-based BSER determinations, and to signal when a state plan revision may be necessary if milestones are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Milestone Report required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Initial Milestone Report (filed five years before planned closure or within 60 days after state plan submission, whichever is later) must include: (1) summary of process steps required to permanently cease operation including timing/duration and notification requirements; (2) list of key milestones with calendar deadlines (must include at least initial notice to relevant reliability authority and submittal of an official retirement filing); (3) analysis comparing the process/timelines to similar EGUs in the state that ceased operations within the prior 10 years; (4) supporting regulatory documents such as correspondence and filings with RTO/ISO/balancing authority/PUC, deactivation-related reliability assessments, SEC filings, integrated resource plans, PUC orders, reliability analyses, and notifications altering timing of deactivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States select certain process steps to serve as milestones; the rule does not require milestones to be taken at particular times, only reporting on intended and actual dates. The Initial Milestone Report provides the baseline against which annual reports will measure progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Milestone Status Report required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each intervening year prior to the planned cessation date, the owner/operator must submit an annual Milestone Status Report addressing: (1) progress toward meeting all milestones identified in the Initial Milestone Report; and (2) supporting regulatory documents and relevant SEC filings (correspondence and filings with RTO/ISO/balancing authority/PUC or other applicable authority) to demonstrate compliance with or progress toward milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports provide ongoing transparency and documentation to the state, EPA, and public on whether the EGU remains on track to permanently cease operations as represented in the state plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Milestone Status Report required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than six months following the committed closure date, the EGU must submit a Final Milestone Status Report documenting actions taken subsequent to ceasing operation to ensure the cessation is permanent, including regulatory filings or decommissioning plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This final report documents whether cessation is permanent and should include any filings with applicable authorities or evidence of decommissioning activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting requirement for milestone reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs with reporting milestones for commitments to permanently cease operations must post their Initial Milestone Report, annual Milestone Status Reports, and Final Milestone Status Report, including the schedule for achieving milestones and any documentation necessary to demonstrate milestones have been achieved, on the Carbon Pollution Standards for EGUs website within 30 business days of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posting requirement aims to make milestone information publicly accessible and to allow stakeholders to assess progress. The rule recognizes jurisdictional differences and allows states to explain how their closure processes satisfy required reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emissions monitoring and reporting requirements (40 CFR part 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs must monitor and report hourly CO2 mass emissions to the atmosphere, total heat input, and total gross electricity output (including useful thermal output converted to gross MWh) using a 40 CFR part 75 certified monitoring methodology and report hourly data on a quarterly basis, with each quarterly report due to the Administrator 30 days after the last day of the calendar quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most coal-fired boilers are required to use a CO2 continuous emissions monitoring system (CEMS) including CO2 concentration and stack gas flow monitors. Some oil- and gas-fired boilers may use alternative measurement methodologies (e.g., fuel flow meters combined with fuel quality data). Relying on part 75-certified monitors reduces implementation costs and ensures consistent emissions data across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS quality assurance and measurement accuracy expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: CO2 CEMS must undergo regular quality assurance and quality control activities including periodic relative accuracy test audits (RATAs) comparing the monitoring system to independent systems using EPA reference methods and NIST-traceable calibration gases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's May 2022 study found the absolute value of the median difference between EGU monitoring systems and independent systems was approximately 2 percent for CO2 concentration monitors and stack gas flow monitors for 2017–2021. EPA disagrees that part 75 data are biased significantly high or low given QA/QC requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS-specific monitoring and GHGRP reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected EGUs employing CCS that capture enough CO2 to meet the standard and inject captured CO2 underground must report under GHGRP subpart RR or GHGRP subpart VV; if the emitting EGU sends captured CO2 offsite, it must transfer the CO2 to a facility subject to GHGRP requirements, and the injecting facility must report under GHGRP subpart RR or VV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with the standard is determined exclusively by the tons of CO2 captured by the emitting EGU (not tons sequestered). The requirement to transfer captured CO2 to an entity subject to GHGRP is an enforcement element to verify transfer and avoid duplicative monitoring. These emission guidelines do not change requirements to obtain or comply with UIC permits; existing geologic sequestration regulatory requirements remain separate from this rule. The BSER is adequately demonstrated based on geologic sequestration not associated with EOR, though EGUs may send CO2 to EOR facilities that report under subpart RR or VV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance and limits for state-level compliance flexibilities (averaging/trading/mass-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: States are permitted to include compliance flexibilities (e.g., emission trading, averaging, unit-specific mass-based compliance) in state plans, provided the use of such flexibilities results in an aggregate level of emission reduction equivalent to each source individually achieving its standard of performance; EPA may limit flexibilities where necessary to protect environmental outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments showed stakeholder interest in mass-based mechanisms for reliability reasons, but the final guidelines recognize that fewer steam generating EGUs may limit the usefulness of certain flexibilities. States must design flexibilities to preserve the intended environmental outcomes of the emission guidelines and ensure aggregate equivalence.
